decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elevated approach to basket handle, gradually pitching gripper downward; keep right arm clear.
Retry basket approach with halved increments after zero-step continuity rejection.
Raise and advance left gripper above moving basket, completing most downward pitch before contact.
Approach basket's left longitudinal rim from above, using downward fingers to straddle it without crossing center.
Track basket's moving left rim with smaller joint-continuous increments, lowering open fingers toward rim height.
Lower fingertips around left rim, close while matching belt motion, then begin a small lift to test retention.
Basket visibly follows closed left fingers; lift another 11 cm and slightly left. Start right gripper's elevated downward approach for target pickup.
Raise basket farther while moving slightly forward to reduce folded-joint demand; continue right-arm preparation. Basket tilt needs monitoring.
Retract basket toward robot and lift gently to regain reach margin after IK failure; no forward motion was executed.
Counter-rotate tilted basket while retracting left arm for reach margin. Prepare right arm above its conveyor workspace; tan figure appears to match board.
Continue slow basket counter-rotation and observe whether it levels or pivots at the rim; finish right downward orientation safely above belt.
Basket is visibly no longer retained. Clear both grippers to let it settle, repositioning left toward target and right above basket's right workspace.
Use smaller rotation increments after continuity rejection; clear basket and prepare to reassess its handle and target.
Basket has settled nearly upright. Align right fingers over its right rim while left returns to downward orientation above the tan target's lane.
Close right fingers around basket's near-right rim and test a small lift; left hovers above matching tan object without grasping yet.
Right pinch appears empty: reopen and advance toward actual right rim. Align left open fingers over tan figure torso, tracking belt motion.
Pinch the visually aligned right rim and test retention with a short retracting lift. Left follows tan target without closing until basket lift is established.
Test basket retention with a 9 cm retracting lift, retaining closed right grip. Left tracks target with slight clearance; verify basket motion from RGB.
Basket did not follow the test lift. Reopen and approach farther forward and lower to put rim between the pads rather than at their tips.
Rotate right pinch direction across the near rim instead of along it, with open pads and gentle belt tracking.
Lower right wrist to improve reach margin and put front rim deeply between crosswise pads; close for another controlled retention test.
Avoid extending wrist farther: retract and tilt fingers forward into front rim, closing once angled pads straddle it. Left retracts for reach margin.
Reduce right tilt to 0.015 radians per step near reach boundary; maintain open pads until alignment is visible.
Pinch front rim crosswise at current alignment, then retract and raise for visual retention check; left keeps pace with target.
Correct visual offset: advance right fingers farther into near rim at lower height. Center left on the board-matching figurine before it leaves left workspace.
Close around figurine torso and crosswise basket rim after a final small forward descent, then test both with a short lift while retracting.
Close at the latest accepted positions, then retract with a small lift to test actual retention without additional forward reach.
Both test grasps were empty. Clear left arm; right advances angled fingers to the basket's visible near-left corner with lower wrist height for reach margin.
Use wrist view to shift the right pinch onto the near basket corner, adding forward reach through tilt and closing only after alignment.
Test the corner pinch by lifting 10 cm while retracting toward a comfortable right-arm position; verify basket follows in RGB.
Empty pinch again. Change to a lower, more forward-pointing side approach to basket's nearest rim instead of reaching downward from too high.
Shift right toward the basket edge seen beside the pad, close around the lip, and test only a small retracting lift.
Use head-calibrated rim estimate farther right and slightly higher; align forward-pointing pads on the basket's leftmost lip before closing.
Finish closing and retract upward to test the latest rim contact. Keep left arm clear.
Correct for link6-to-pad offset: approach substantially farther forward and lower so basket lip reaches the pad centers, not merely the fingertip line.
Make small wrist-view corrections toward the elevated rim, flattening finger approach and closing after alignment; avoid a large joint jump.
Shift the open pinch toward the lip on the right side of the wrist image, with small lateral/upward corrections before closing.
At reach boundary, redirect fingers outward and upward toward the visible lip rather than translating the wrist farther out; then close.
Finish closing on the rim now visible between the jaws, then pull inward with a small lift to check retention and restore reach margin.
Keep the pinch closed and draw it inward/upward; basket material is visible between jaws, but retention remains uncertain until it returns to head view.
Basket was not retained. Reorient fingers outward toward its departing left rim while keeping wrist lower and within right workspace.
Basket is clearly visible ahead in right wrist view. Advance open jaws toward its near lip while lowering wrist to retain elbow-up reach margin.
Lower the right wrist and point fingers more outward toward the basket's near end, approaching in small continuous increments without crossing arms.
Basket has moved beyond comfortable reach. Retract right arm toward the identified tan figurine while pitching fingers down, preventing the target from leaving reachable workspace.
Use reduced translation and pitch increments after continuity rejection, retracting from reach boundary toward the target.
Align right gripper with figurine rather than adjacent remote, continuing downward pitch and compensating for finger offset and belt motion.
Figurine is beside the right pads; adjust slightly back/down while tracking belt, close on torso, then make a short retention-test lift.
The figurine lies beyond the closed tips. Reopen and advance deeper around its lower torso, then close while matching conveyor drift.
Figurine is visibly between pads. Keep closed and retract/lift into right workspace, verifying it moves with the gripper.
Retry target lift with smaller increments after zero-step continuity rejection; retain closed right gripper.
Target was not retained. Reopen and align lower and farther right, keeping wrist back so pads meet torso rather than overshooting its conveyor lane.
Raise pad contact toward the upright figurine's torso, with a flatter approach to avoid grasping below the body.
Advance along the finger direction so the figurine's lower torso reaches between the pads, then close while tracking conveyor motion.
Replan from the interrupted pose: shift down and inward toward the figurine's image offset instead of extending farther, then close in place.
Target remains beyond the pinch. Reopen and redirect fingers outward with a flatter side approach, avoiding further downward reach near joint limits.
Make a small inward/downward alignment toward torso, close without extending farther, and test a gentle retracting lift.
Target and basket have moved beyond safe reach and neither is retained. Retract right arm to regain margin while monitoring conveyor for another opportunity.
Continue safe retraction and return right gripper toward a forward/downward orientation, monitoring for objects reentering reachable conveyor space.
Retract both empty grippers into their own workspaces, retaining elbow-up configuration and watching for a reachable basket or target.
